result.topic_en: Summary account of how the isoperimetric/maximum-minimum problem, posed purely analytically for the integral of V dx, was first solved by pure analysis by Lagrange of Turin, prompting Euler to found the calculus of variations, which differs from the differential calculus in its manner of treatment.

items.quote: vt data quantitate V vtcunque ex binis variabilibus $x$, $y$, earumque differentialibus cuiuscunque ordinis, quin etiam ex formulis integralibus vtcunque conflata, ea inter $x$ et $y$ relatio inuestigari debeat, qua formulae integrali $\int V\,dx$ maximus minimusue valor concilietur?
items.english: that, given a quantity V composed in any way of two variables x, y and their differentials of any order, and even of integral formulas, that relation between x and y should be found by which the integral formula ∫V dx obtains a maximum or minimum value?

items.quote: quem \textit{Calculum variationum} appellat, et cuius elementa hic tradere ac dilucide explicare constituit.
items.english: which he calls the Calculus of variations, and whose elements he has resolved to present and clearly explain here.
